questions.title: Safe oxygen therapy
questions.question: Before starting prescribed oxygen via nasal cannula, which assessment should the nurse prioritise?
options: Inspect the nasal passages and assess respiratory status
Offer the patient a glass of water
Place the patient flat in bed
questions.rationale: A baseline respiratory assessment and checking the nares support safe application and later reassessment of oxygen therapy.
questions.sourceTitle: British Thoracic Society guideline for oxygen use in adults (2017)
questions.learningObjective: Assess first, apply safely, then reassess the response.
questions.visualBrief: Simulated ward setting; nurse checks nasal cannula equipment and observation chart, no readable patient information.

questions.title: Recognising deterioration
questions.question: Which action is most appropriate when a patient shows signs of possible sepsis and clinical deterioration?
options: Escalate urgently using the local deterioration pathway
Wait until the next routine observations
Give oral fluids and review tomorrow
Document it only after the shift ends
questions.rationale: New confusion, fever and increased respiratory rate require timely assessment and escalation under local policy.
questions.sourceTitle: NICE guideline NG51: Sepsis: recognition, diagnosis and early management
questions.learningObjective: A changing patient needs timely escalation—not watchful waiting.
questions.visualBrief: Simulated nurse identifies changing observations and uses an escalation call bell; no patient body or clinical procedure.

questions.title: Clean hands, safer care
questions.question: When should hand hygiene be performed during preparation for an aseptic procedure?
options: At the end of the shift
Only if hands look visibly soiled
questions.rationale: Hand hygiene immediately before an aseptic task helps prevent microorganisms reaching a vulnerable site.
questions.sourceTitle: WHO: My 5 Moments for Hand Hygiene
questions.learningObjective: Know the moment: before touching the patient and before an aseptic task.
questions.visualBrief: Clean simulation hands and sink station; show preparation, not an invasive procedure.

questions.title: Pause before administration
questions.question: A medication label does not match the electronic prescription. What should the nurse do first?
options: Stop and clarify the discrepancy before administration
Administer the labelled dose to avoid delay
Ask the patient which dose they usually take
questions.rationale: Do not administer when a discrepancy is present. Pause, verify the order and follow local medicines-management procedures.
questions.learningObjective: A mismatch is a stop signal—clarify before giving medicine.
questions.visualBrief: Simulated medication trolley with deliberately blurred labels and a nurse pausing to verify; no drug names or dosage instructions.
